KEN.note: The only AI item is a student charged under the general false-publication offence for an AI-generated image; the document does not say a rule on AI harms applies.

facts.fact: CPJ says Kenya's 2018 Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act took effect after a 2020 High Court ruling, with October amendments giving a national cybercrime committee power to ban sites and apps.
Journalist Peter Mwita was charged in a Mombasa court under the cybercrimes law over a WhatsApp message and pleaded not guilty; CPJ lists other bloggers and journalists arrested under it.

KEN.note: The document states nothing about a data protection law.

facts.fact: CPJ says journalist Peter Mwita was detained seven days from 31 December and charged on 25 February 2026 over a WhatsApp message alleging links between a Mombasa politician and a gang.
The Blogger Association of Kenya argues in a constitutional appeal that the 2018 cybercrimes law violates freedom of expression, with a ruling due 27 February 2026.
